justification: Same inputs, attention and logits are bit-identical. CPU FP32 log_softmax and selected-logit-minus-logsumexp differ by up to 1.775e-5 per token over 4-130 scored tokens. A length-independent 2e-5 bound on their sums is too stringent for these kernels. The 2e-5 per-token allowance and standard sequential summation bound are explicit length-aware qualifications. Actual installed TRL with FP64 reductions on the same FP32 logits restores score/loss agreement and gradients below the original FP32 2e-6 bound. A single doubled FP32 gradient bound (4e-6) accommodates the empirically isolated score arithmetic; it is an empirical fixture tolerance, not a universal numerical theorem. No production scoring code, examples or training data changed.
loss_bound: beta times the sum of chosen and rejected score bounds; softplus is 1-Lipschitz
scope: Post-failure numerical adjudication on these fixed eight state/example cases. Original absolute-tolerance parity did not pass. No full Trainer equivalence.
score_bound: N*2e-5 + gamma_(N-1)*sum(abs(FP64 token log probabilities)); gamma_k=k*eps/(1-k*eps), eps=2^-23
